IPC::Response_FunctionsT save_weld_parameter(const std::string &robot_model, int dev_id, int dev_ip_0, int dev_ip_1, int dev_ip_2, int dev_ip_3, int dev_port, int out_pno_arc, int out_pno_touch, int out_pno_gas, int out_pno_inch, int out_pno_reinch, int out_pno_current, int out_pno_voltage, int in_pno_ready, int in_pno_arc, int in_pno_touch, int in_pno_gas, int in_pno_feeder, int in_pno_error, int in_pno_current, int in_pno_voltage, int hw_process_type, int hw_wire_type, int hw_wire_size, int hw_gas_type, std::vector<float> current_map_value, std::vector<float> current_map_output, std::vector<float> voltage_map_value, std::vector<float> voltage_map_output, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Saves the welding device configuration (Settings > Devices > Welding).

Configures which digital/analog I/O ports the welding device is wired to, and the current/voltage conversion maps used to translate a requested welding current/voltage into the corresponding raw analog output value (and vice versa for feedback). Read back with call_config_weld.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • dev_id – Welding device type. 0 = None, 1 = I/O Signal.

  • dev_ip_0 – First octet of the welding device IP address.

  • dev_ip_1 – Second octet of the welding device IP address.

  • dev_ip_2 – Third octet of the welding device IP address.

  • dev_ip_3 – Fourth octet of the welding device IP address.

  • dev_port – Communication port of the welding device.

  • out_pno_arc – Digital output port number for the Arc On signal. -1 = none, 0-15 = Digital Output 0-15.

  • out_pno_touch – Digital output port number for the Touch On signal. -1 = none, 0-15 = Digital Output 0-15.

  • out_pno_gas – Digital output port number for the Gas On signal. -1 = none, 0-15 = Digital Output 0-15.

  • out_pno_inch – Digital output port number for the Wire Inch signal. -1 = none, 0-15 = Digital Output 0-15.

  • out_pno_reinch – Digital output port number for the Wire Re-Inch signal. -1 = none, 0-15 = Digital Output 0-15.

  • out_pno_current – Analog output port number for the current setting. -1 = none, 0-3 = Analog Output 0-3.

  • out_pno_voltage – Analog output port number for the voltage setting. -1 = none, 0-3 = Analog Output 0-3.

  • in_pno_ready – Digital input port number for the Welder Ready feedback signal. -1 = none, 0-15 = Digital Input 0-15.

  • in_pno_arc – Digital input port number for the Arc Generated feedback signal. -1 = none, 0-15 = Digital Input 0-15.

  • in_pno_touch – Digital input port number for the Touch Signal feedback. -1 = none, 0-15 = Digital Input 0-15.

  • in_pno_gas – Digital input port number for the Gas Signal feedback. -1 = none, 0-15 = Digital Input 0-15.

  • in_pno_feeder – Digital input port number for the Feeder Signal feedback. -1 = none, 0-15 = Digital Input 0-15.

  • in_pno_error – Digital input port number for the Welder Error signal. -1 = none, 0-15 = Digital Input 0-15.

  • in_pno_current – Analog input port number for the current feedback. -1 = none, 0-3 = Analog Input 0-3.

  • in_pno_voltage – Analog input port number for the voltage feedback. -1 = none, 0-3 = Analog Input 0-3.

  • current_map_value – Input (raw) value list for the welding current conversion map.

  • current_map_output – Output (converted) value list for the welding current conversion map, paired index-for-index with current_map_value.

  • voltage_map_value – Input (raw) value list for the welding voltage conversion map.

  • voltage_map_output – Output (converted) value list for the welding voltage conversion map, paired index-for-index with voltage_map_value.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronously) once the response is received, provided its return_value is 0; a nonzero return_value raises before flow_manager_args.done() is reached.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or no payload is returned.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the save result.

IPC::Response_FunctionsT call_move_macro(const std::string &robot_model, int type, std::vector<MoveTargetValuesArg> corner_pnts, std::optional<MoveSpeedArg> speed, int rotation_mode, int gap_num, float margin_h_1, float margin_h_2, float margin_w_1, float margin_w_2, float margin_over, float margin_over_para, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Runs a Motion Macro: a pre-built multi-segment move pattern (flat surface / round / triangle / 3D round) derived from a small set of corner points.

Rounds each point in corner_pnts to 3 decimal places, pads or truncates it to the 7-value tar_values format expected by the firmware, and forwards the request. The number of points required in corner_pnts depends on type: Flat Surface = 4, Round (R) = 6, Round (H) = 6, Triangle = 3, 3D Round = 9.

Note

If flow_manager_args is provided, this function returns immediately after submitting the request; a background monitor waits for the actual motion-completion signal from the robot before invoking the flow manager’s completion callback.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • type – Motion Macro type. 0 = Flat Surface, 1 = Round (R), 2 = Round (H), 3 = Triangle, 4 = 3D Round.

  • corner_pnts – Corner points defining the macro shape, each a [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz, aa]-style value list (up to 7 elements; shorter lists are zero-padded). The number of points required depends on type (see above).

  • speed – Movement speed parameters used to run the macro.

  • rotation_mode – Orientation option. 0 = Intended, 1 = Constant.

  • gap_num – Gap number between macro segments.

  • margin_h_1 – Margin height 1 (mm).

  • margin_h_2 – Margin height 2 (mm).

  • margin_w_1 – Margin width 1 (mm).

  • margin_w_2 – Margin width 2 (mm).

  • margin_over – Margin over (mm).

  • margin_over_para – Margin over parameter, in the range [0, 1].

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, the macro’s motion result is reported to the flow manager and completion is handled asynchronously.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or no payload is returned.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the macro-start result.

Stops an active repeating Pattern by ID.

  • id – Pattern ID to stop, in the range [0, 29].

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronously) once the response is received, provided its return_value is 0; a nonzero return_value raises before flow_manager_args.done() is reached.

IPC::Response_FunctionsT call_pattern_on(const std::string &robot_model, int id, int type, std::optional<std::vector<MoveTargetValuesArg>> corner_pnts, std::optional<std::vector<MoveTargetValuesArg>> random_pnts, int count_x, int count_y, int count_z, MoveTargetValuesArg anchor_pnt, int incremental, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Starts a repeating Pattern move: a grid or randomized sweep of points around an anchor point.

Builds the target point list from corner_pnts (for Line / Plane / Cube patterns) or random_pnts (when type is 3, Random), rounding each point to 3 decimal places and padding/truncating it to the 7-value tar_values format. The number of points required in corner_pnts depends on type: Line (X) = 2, Plane (X-Y) = 4, Cube (X-Y-Z) = 8; Random patterns instead take random_pnts, whose point count is caller-defined. Call call_pattern_off to stop.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • id – Pattern ID to run, in the range [0, 29]. Running a new pattern on an ID already in use is expected to replace it.

  • type – Pattern type. 0 = Line (X), 1 = Plane (X-Y), 2 = Cube (X-Y-Z), 3 = Random.

  • corner_pnts – Corner points defining the pattern grid, each a [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz, aa]-style value list (up to 7 elements; shorter lists are zero-padded). Used when type is not 3 (Random); ignored otherwise.

  • random_pnts – Explicit point list used only when type is 3 (Random), in the same per-point format as corner_pnts. Ignored for the other pattern types.

  • count_x – Number of points to generate along the X axis.

  • count_y – Number of points to generate along the Y axis.

  • count_z – Number of points to generate along the Z axis.

  • anchor_pnt – Reference point the pattern grid is built around, as a [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz, aa]-style value list (up to 7 elements; shorter lists are zero-padded).

  • incremental – Whether the pattern advances incrementally between activations (nonzero) or restarts from the first point each time (0).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronously) once the response is received, provided its return_value is 0; a nonzero return_value raises before flow_manager_args.done() is reached.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or no payload is returned.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the pattern-start result.

Runs automatic TCP position calibration from a set of joint poses (Move > Calibration > TCP Position).

The robot is moved through the given joint poses and the TCP offset is computed from the resulting motion. Each entry in joints is rounded to 3 decimal places and padded/truncated to 7 values before being sent.

IPC::Response_FunctionsT call_gripper_action(const std::string &robot_model, int gripper_type, int function_list, std::vector<float> payload, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Sends an Initialize command, plus any additional configured commands (e.g., Set-position, Action), to a configured gripper or end-of-arm tool.

A single generic entry point for all supported gripper models (Dynamixel, DH PG/CG/AG, Robotiq E-Pick/2F/Hand-E, Baumer LDS, OnRobot 2FG/RG/3FG/VG/VGC/MG/SoftGripper/VGP20/Sander, JRT JEG series, and others). function_list is model-specific: index 0 is always Initialize, and later indices are model-specific actions (e.g. Set Goal Position, Set Goal Pos/Spd/Force, Reset, Suction). The meaning of each payload slot depends on both gripper_type and function_list — each of the 23 supported gripper types has its own per-function payload layout (slot index, unit, and default value), too large to reproduce here in full; consult the gripper’s setup UI or vendor documentation for the exact slot mapping of the model in use.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • gripper_type – Gripper/tool model selector. 0 = Dynamixel Motor, 1 = DH PG/CG Series, 2 = DH AG Series, 3 = Robotiq E-Pick, 4 = Robotiq 2F Series, 5 = Robotiq Hand-E Series, 6 = Baumer LDS, 7 = OnRobot 2FG7, 8 = OnRobot 2FG14, 9 = OnRobot RG2, 10 = OnRobot RG6, 11 = OnRobot 3FG15, 12 = OnRobot 3FG25, 13 = OnRobot VG10, 14 = OnRobot VGC10, 15 = OnRobot MG10, 16 = OnRobot SoftGripper, 17 = OnRobot VGP20, 18 = OnRobot Sander, 19 = JRT JEGB, 20 = JRT JEGG, 21 = JRT JEGC, 22 = JRT JEGH.

  • function_list – Action to run for the selected gripper_type. 0 is Initialize for every model; the meaning of other indices is model-specific (see schema).

  • payload – Positional argument list for the selected gripper_type / function_list combination (e.g. connection port, device ID, target position/speed/force). Layout is model- and function-specific — see schema.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronously) once the response is received, provided its return_value is 0; a nonzero return_value raises before flow_manager_args.done() is reached.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or no payload is returned.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the command result.

IPC::Response_CallConfigSoftPLCT call_config_softplc(const std::string &robot_model, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Reads the saved Software PLC rule table (Settings > Devices > Software PLC).

Returns the configuration of all 32 Software PLC rule slots. Each slot is a simple ladder-logic-style rule: “IF (Input A) [operator]

(Input B) THEN (Output)”, evaluated while the slot’s mode condition holds — see

save_softplc_parameter for field semantics. Every response field is a length-32 array indexed by PLC slot number.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronously) after the response is received.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or no payload is returned.

Returns:

IPC::Response_CallConfigSoftPLCT containing the 32 saved rule slots (one entry per array index).

IPC::Response_FunctionsT save_softplc_parameter(const std::string &robot_model, int plcnum, int mode, int operation, int input_a_type, int input_a_select, int input_b_type, int input_b_select, int output_type, int output_select, int output_value, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Saves one Software PLC rule slot (Settings > Devices > Software PLC).

Configures a ladder-logic-style rule: “IF (Input A) [operation]

(Input B) THEN (Output)”, active while the

mode condition holds. The meaning of input_a_select / input_b_select / output_select depends on the paired input_a_type / input_b_type / output_type — see apps/web/nexus/src/constants/software-plc-opts.c.ts in the frontend repo for the full per-type option index tables (I/O signal numbers, system status/parameter indices, data field indices, output signal numbers, etc.).

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • plcnum – PLC rule slot to configure, in the range [0, 31].

  • mode – Condition under which the rule is active. 0 = Power Off, 1 = Always, 2 = Idle, 3 = Playing, 4 = Moving.

  • operation – Operator combining Input A and Input B. 0 = ==, 1 = !=, 2 = >, 3 = <, 4 = >=, 5 = <=, 6 = logical AND, 7 = logical OR, 8 = + (add), 9 = x (multiply), 10 = bitwise AND, 11 = bitwise OR.

  • input_a_type – Category of Input A. 0 = I/O Signal, 1 = System Status, 2 = System Parameter, 3 = Data Communication, 4 = Data Dummy, 5 = Signal Level, 6 = User Number (literal value).

  • input_a_select – Index within input_a_type's option list selecting Input A (or, when input_a_type is 6, the literal value itself).

  • input_b_type – Category of Input B, same encoding as input_a_type.

  • input_b_select – Index within input_b_type's option list selecting Input B (or the literal value, as with input_a_select).

  • output_type – Category of the rule’s Output. 0 = Signal Output, 1 = Ex System Function, 2 = Value Substitution, 3 = Value Direct Enter.

  • output_select – Index within output_type's option list selecting the output target.

  • output_value – Literal value written to the output when output_type is 3 (Value Direct Enter).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronously) once the response is received, provided its return_value is 0; a nonzero return_value raises before flow_manager_args.done() is reached.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If the query fails or no payload is returned.

Returns:

IPC::Response_FunctionsT containing the save result.

class RBManipulateStateSDK : public RBBaseSDK#

Public Functions

inline RBManipulateStateSDK()#
IPC::State_CoreT state_core(const std::string &robot_model)#

Retrieves the latest published core state snapshot of the robot.

Waits for and returns the most recent message on the robot’s state_core topic, which carries joint/Cartesian references and encoder readings, tool and I/O state, motion status, and force/torque data. This is the same topic that call_move_j and the other move functions in RBManipulateMoveSDK subscribe to internally in order to detect motion completion via motion_sub_index and timestamp_usec_mono.

Parameters:

robot_model – Name of the robot model. A single, non-wildcard model name is required.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If robot_model contains a wildcard (*) character.

Returns:

IPC::State_CoreT containing the current state snapshot.

std::vector<IPC::Response_CallWhoamIT> call_whoami(const std::string &robot_model, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Requests identification information from the robot.

Queries the robot for its category, model name, firmware version, and alias. robot_model may be a zenoh key-expression that matches more than one robot (unlike state_core, which rejects wildcards); each matching robot returns its own reply, so the result is a list with one entry per robot instead of a single response.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model. May be a key-expression matching multiple robots.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context, accepted for API consistency with the other functions in this class; this function never reports completion through it (it always returns synchronously with the query result).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If no robot replies before the timeout.

Returns:

List of IPC::Response_CallWhoamIT, one per robot that replied.

std::vector<IPC::Response_FunctionsT> call_powercontrol(const std::string &robot_model, const int power_option, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Requests the cobot to turn its main power on or off.

robot_model may be a zenoh key-expression that matches more than one robot; each matching robot returns its own reply, so the result is a list with one entry per robot instead of a single response.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model. May be a key-expression matching multiple robots.

  • power_option – Power state value. 0 = power off, 1 = power on (with the normal pre-power-on check), 2 = power on without that check (labeled “force on” in the operator UI). Any other value is treated as power off.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once every matched robot has replied.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If no robot replies before the timeout.

Returns:

List of IPC::Response_FunctionsT, one per robot that replied.

std::vector<IPC::Response_FunctionsT> call_servocontrol(const std::string &robot_model, const int servo_option, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Requests the cobot to turn its servo on.

Every accepted value of servo_option turns the servo on; there is no value that turns it off through this call (main power must be turned off via call_powercontrol to de-energize the motors).

robot_model may be a zenoh key-expression that matches more than one robot; each matching robot returns its own reply, so the result is a list with one entry per robot instead of a single response.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model. May be a key-expression matching multiple robots.

  • servo_option – Servo-on mode. 0 = basic servo-on, 1 = basic servo-on plus reference-on, 2 = emergency teaching (hand guiding) mode. Any other value is treated as 0.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once every matched robot has replied.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If no robot replies before the timeout.

Returns:

List of IPC::Response_FunctionsT, one per robot that replied.

std::vector<IPC::Response_FunctionsT> call_referencecontrol(const std::string &robot_model, const int reference_option, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Requests the cobot to switch between simulation and real operation reference.

Turning the reference on requires the servo to already be fully on; the request is rejected otherwise. When turned on, the robot’s internal motion reference is re-initialized from the current encoder position of every joint.

robot_model may be a zenoh key-expression that matches more than one robot; each matching robot returns its own reply, so the result is a list with one entry per robot instead of a single response.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model. May be a key-expression matching multiple robots.

  • reference_option – Robot operation reference value. 0 = Simulation (operates in simulation mode), 1 = Real (operates the actual robot).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, completion is reported to the flow manager immediately (synchronous) once every matched robot has replied.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If no robot replies before the timeout.

Returns:

List of IPC::Response_FunctionsT, one per robot that replied.

void publish_state_core(const std::string &robot_model, const IPC::State_CoreT &state_core)#

Publishes a core state message on the robot’s state_core topic.

Publishes state_core to {robot_model}/state_core, the same topic that state_core reads from and that call_move_j and the other move functions in RBManipulateMoveSDK subscribe to for detecting motion completion. On a live robot this topic is normally published to periodically by the robot’s own firmware; calling this against a live robot’s topic competes with that periodic publish.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • state_core – State snapshot to publish.

mechmind::MechMindClient *execute_mechmind_connect(const std::string &module_name, muscat::InterfaceMechMindPayloadT data, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args, AlarmFn alarm_fn)#

Connects to a MechMind vision server and registers the client under module_name.

Reads connection parameters from data (server_ip, server_port, an optional timeout_sec defaulting to 10 seconds, an optional project_id defaulting to 1) and opens a MechMind TCP connection, storing the resulting client in the per-module connection registry so later calls (trigger, get_poses, …) can look it up by the same module_name.

Note

If the native connect call fails without throwing (client non-null but not connected), that failure is only logged to stdout — it does not go through resolve_option’s SKIP/STOP/ASK handling, unlike an actual vendor exception.

Note

Calling this again with the same module_name transparently disconnects the previous client for that module before opening the new connection.

Parameters:

  • module_name – Registry key for the connection, normally the PyFM task id resolved from flow_manager_args.

  • data – Connect payload. Must contain server_ip and server_port; timeout_sec and project_id are optional.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. When provided, flow_manager_args.done() is called unconditionally once the connection attempt finishes, even if it failed.

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when data's resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If server_ip or server_port is missing, or if resolve_option is invalid; and, if resolve_option is “STOP”, if the native connect call throws.

Returns:

Pointer to the connected mechmind::MechMindClient, owned by the SDK’s connection registry (do not delete it). May be null, or non-null but not connected, if the attempt failed.

mechmind::VisionResponse execute_mechmind_trigger_and_get_poses(mechmind::MechMindClient *client, int project_id, const std::string &position, const std::string &return_variable_name, std::optional<IPC::State_CoreT> state_core = std::nullopt, const std::string &resolve_option = "SKIP", FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr)#

Triggers a MechMind capture + recognition and reads the detected poses in one round-trip.

Standalone equivalent of function_code=0 (“Trigger And Get Poses”) of the MechMind READ interface. When position is “EYE_TO_HAND” the camera is fixed off the robot, so no robot-pose correction is sent. Otherwise (position is “EYE_IN_HEAD”) the camera is mounted on the robot, so the current TCP pose, joint positions and tool TCP offset (all derived from state_core) are sent so the vendor can correct for the arm’s current pose.

Parameters:

  • client – Connected MechMind client, e.g. from execute_mechmind_connect.

  • project_id – MechMind project id to trigger against.

  • position – “EYE_TO_HAND” or “EYE_IN_HEAD” — selects whether robot-pose correction is sent, see above.

  • return_variable_name – PyFM variable name that will receive the detected poses as a list of [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz] entries.

  • state_core – Robot state snapshot used for pose correction. Required when position is not “EYE_TO_HAND”.

  • resolve_option – How to handle a client-side failure — client not connected, or the native call throwing a MechMind exception: “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. On success, return_variable_name is written into its context and flow_manager_args.done() is called.

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If position is not “EYE_TO_HAND” and state_core is not provided; and, under “STOP”, if the native call throws.

Returns:

mechmind::VisionResponse with the detected poses. A default-constructed (empty) response if client is null, not connected, or the call failed under “SKIP”/”ASK”.

mechmind::VisionResponse execute_mechmind_get_poses(mechmind::MechMindClient *client, int project_id, const std::string &return_variable_name, const std::string &resolve_option = "SKIP", FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr)#

Reads the poses detected by the most recent MechMind trigger.

Standalone equivalent of function_code=2 (“Get Poses”) of the MechMind READ interface. Unlike execute_mechmind_trigger_and_get_poses, this does not trigger a new capture — it only re-reads the result of whichever trigger (via execute_mechmind_trigger or execute_mechmind_trigger_and_get_poses) ran most recently for project_id.

Parameters:

  • client – Connected MechMind client.

  • project_id – MechMind project id to read poses for.

  • return_variable_name – PyFM variable name that will receive the detected poses as a list of [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz] entries.

  • resolve_option – How to handle a client-side failure — client not connected, or the native call throwing a MechMind exception: “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. On success, return_variable_name is written into its context and flow_manager_args.done() is called.

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – Under “STOP”, if the native call throws.

Returns:

mechmind::VisionResponse with the detected poses. A default-constructed (empty) response if client is null, not connected, or the call failed under “SKIP”/”ASK”.

bool execute_mechmind_trigger(mechmind::MechMindClient *client, int project_id, int expected_count, const std::string &position, std::optional<IPC::State_CoreT> stat_core = std::nullopt, const std::string &resolve_option = "SKIP", FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr)#

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. On success, flow_manager_args.done() is called.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If position is not “EYE_TO_HAND” and stat_core is not provided; and, under “STOP”, if the native call throws.

true on success; false if client is null, not connected, or the call failed under “SKIP”/”ASK” (the native call itself always returns true when it doesn’t throw).

photoneo::PhotoneoClient *execute_photoneo_connect(const std::string &module_name, muscat::InterfacePhotoneoPayloadT data, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args, AlarmFn alarm_fn)#

Connects to a Photoneo Bin Picking Studio (BPS) server and registers the client under module_name.

Reads connection parameters from data (server_ip, server_port, an optional timeout_sec defaulting to 10 seconds) and opens a Photoneo TCP connection, storing the resulting client in the per-module connection registry so later calls (initialize, scan, …) can look it up by the same module_name.

Note

If the native connect call fails without throwing (client non-null but not connected), that failure is only logged to stdout — it does not go through resolve_option’s SKIP/STOP/ASK handling, unlike an actual vendor exception.

Note

Calling this again with the same module_name transparently disconnects the previous client for that module before opening the new connection.

Parameters:

  • module_name – Registry key for the connection, normally the PyFM task id resolved from flow_manager_args.

  • data – Connect payload. Must contain server_ip and server_port; timeout_sec is optional.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. When provided, flow_manager_args.done() is called unconditionally once the connection attempt finishes, even if it failed.

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when data's resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If server_ip or server_port is missing, or if resolve_option is invalid; and, if resolve_option is “STOP”, if the native connect call throws.

Returns:

Pointer to the connected photoneo::PhotoneoClient, owned by the SDK’s connection registry (do not delete it). May be null, or non-null but not connected, if the attempt failed.

photoneo::TrajectoryResponse execute_photoneo_get_trajectory(photoneo::PhotoneoClient *client, uint32_t vision_system_id, const std::string &trajectory_start_to_approach, const std::string &trajectory_approach_to_grasp, const std::string &trajectory_grasp_to_deapproach, const std::string &trajectory_deapproach_to_end, const std::string &resolve_option = "SKIP", FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr)#

Reads the 4-stage pick trajectory computed by the most recent Photoneo scan.

Standalone equivalent of function_code=3 (“Get Trajectory”) of the Photoneo READ interface. Requires a prior successful scan (via execute_photoneo_scan) on vision_system_id. The trajectory is split into exactly four stages — Start->Approach, Approach->Grasp, Grasp->Deapproach, Deapproach->End — and each stage’s joint waypoints are written into its own PyFM variable.

Note

Any gripper-action entries interleaved in the raw trajectory, and the AI Picking INFO values (target bounding-box dimensions), are not extracted by this function — only the 4 segments’ joint waypoints are exposed.

Parameters:

  • client – Connected Photoneo client.

  • vision_system_id – Photoneo vision system id to read the trajectory from. 0 uses the client’s configured default.

  • trajectory_start_to_approach – PyFM variable name that will receive the Start->Approach stage’s waypoints, each a list of joint values.

  • trajectory_approach_to_grasp – Same, for Approach->Grasp.

  • trajectory_grasp_to_deapproach – Same, for Grasp->Deapproach.

  • trajectory_deapproach_to_end – Same, for Deapproach->End.

  • resolve_option – How to handle a client-side failure — client not connected, or the native call throwing a Photoneo exception: “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. On success, the four stage variables above are written into its context and flow_manager_args.done() is called.

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If the response does not contain exactly 4 trajectory segments; and, under “STOP”, if the native call throws.

Returns:

photoneo::TrajectoryResponse with the raw response. A default-constructed (empty) response if client is null, not connected, or the call failed under “SKIP”/”ASK”.

void execute_photoneo_move_waypoints(std::vector<std::vector<double>> waypoints, const std::string &robot_model, int robot_axis_count, int pnt_type, float pnt_para, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr)#

Moves the robot through an already-resolved list of joint waypoints via a JB (joint-blend) move.

Unlike the vendor-facing execute_photoneo_* functions above, this does not talk to a Photoneo client at all — it drives the robot itself through waypoints using RBManipulateMoveSDK::call_move_jb_clr / call_move_jb_add / call_move_jb_run (clear the pending blend queue, add each waypoint, then run). It is the execution half of function_code=8 (“Move (JB)”) of the Photoneo interface; callers that already have a resolved waypoint list (as opposed to a PyFM trajectory variable name) can call it directly instead of going through vision().

Each waypoint is converted from Photoneo’s fixed 6-axis trajectory format to the robot’s actual robot_axis_count: reduced to 6 axes if given more (dropping the third element), then, if the robot has 7 or more axes, expanded back to 7 by inserting 0 at index 2.

Note

Every waypoint is sent with a fixed tar_frame=-1 (Joint Space) and tar_unit=0 (degree) — this is not currently configurable through this function.

Note

Unlike the vendor-facing execute_* functions, there is no resolve_option here: any move failure always raises (and fires alarm_fn, if provided) rather than being SKIP/STOP/ASK-gated.

Parameters:

  • waypoints – Non-empty list of joint-value sequences (a Python list/tuple or numpy 2D array is accepted), in Photoneo’s 6-axis trajectory order.

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model to move.

  • robot_axis_count – Number of axes the target robot actually has; controls the 6-to-N axis expansion described above.

  • pnt_type – Blend type for every waypoint: 0 = Percentage, 1 = Distance.

  • pnt_para – Blend parameter for every waypoint, in the unit implied by pnt_type (percent, or millimeters).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. On success, flow_manager_args.done() is called once after the final move request (call_move_jb_run) is accepted — not after the robot physically finishes the move.

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback fired, with title “Vision(Photoneo) Move Failed”, if any of the clr/add/run requests reports a nonzero return value.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If waypoints is empty, or if any clr/add/run request reports a nonzero return value (the first such failure stops the sequence immediately — later waypoints are never sent).

Configures the Pickit3D robot-camera calibration procedure.

Standalone equivalent of function_code=4 (“Configure Calib”) of the Pickit WRITE interface. The robot TCP pose and tool TCP offset (derived from stat_core) are always sent, but are only meaningful to Pickit for the SINGLE_POSE/MANUAL calibration methods — other methods ignore them.

Parameters:

  • client – Connected Pickit client.

  • calib_method – Pickit calibration method id — see pickit3d::CalibrationMethod (constants.hpp), payload[0] of the native RC_PICKIT_CONFIGURE_CALIB(11) command: 0=SINGLE_POSE, 1=MULTI_POSE, 2=MANUAL, 3=DEFAULT. The caller (program step) may also pass the matching label string (“SINGLE_POSE”, “MULTI_POSE”, “MANUAL”, “DEFAULT”) — rb_vision_util::get_calib_method resolves it to this id before the call reaches here.

  • calib_camera_mount – Camera mount id — 0=FIXED (Eye-to-Hand — camera fixed in the cell, sees the whole scene) or 1=ON_ROBOT (Eye-in-Hand — camera mounted on the robot flange, moves with it). The caller may also pass “EYE_TO_HAND”/ “FIXED” or “EYE_IN_HAND”/”ON_ROBOT” — rb_vision_util::get_calib_camera_mount resolves the label to this id. Must match how the camera is physically mounted on this cell; this is the same setting that decides whether detection uses execute_pickit_look_for_objects (FIXED) or execute_pickit_capture_image + execute_pickit_process_image (ON_ROBOT).

  • stat_core – Robot state snapshot the TCP pose and tool TCP offset are derived from.

  • resolve_option – How to handle a client-side failure — client not connected, or the native call throwing a Pickit exception: “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. On success, flow_manager_args.done() is called.

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

  • std::runtime_error – Under “STOP”, if the native call throws a Pickit exception.

  • std::invalid_argument – If calib_method is SINGLE_POSE and calib_camera_mount is ON_ROBOT (an unsupported combination). This is not a Pickit protocol exception, so it is not caught by the resolve_option handling above — it always propagates directly to the caller.

Returns:

true on success; false if client is null, not connected, or the call failed under “SKIP”/”ASK”.

Reads the gripper pose computed from the most recent Pickit3D detection.

Standalone equivalent of function_code=12 (“Get Pick Point Data”) of the Pickit READ interface. Takes no robot pose of its own — the client automatically reuses the detected object’s pose cached by the most recent successful execute_pickit_look_for_objects, execute_pickit_look_for_objects_with_retries, execute_pickit_next_object, or execute_pickit_process_image call. The gripper pose is computed by composing that cached detection pose with the response’s offset pose; if no detection pose is cached, the gripper pose is not available.

Parameters:

  • client – Connected Pickit client.

  • gripper_pose_name – PyFM variable name that will receive the computed gripper pose as a 6-element [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz] list, or None if no cached detection pose is available.

  • reference_pick_point_id_name – PyFM variable name that will receive the reference pick point id from the response.

  • stat_core – Robot state snapshot the tool TCP offset is derived from (no TCP pose is sent — see above).

  • resolve_option – How to handle a client-side failure — client not connected, or the native call throwing a Pickit exception: “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. On success, the two variables above are written into its context and flow_manager_args.done() is called.

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – Under “STOP”, if the native call throws.

Returns:

pickit3d::PickPointData with the pick point result. A default-constructed (empty) result if client is null, not connected, or the call failed under “SKIP”/”ASK”.

void vision(const std::string &robot_model, const std::string &option, muscat::VisionInterfacePayloadUnion data, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Single dispatch entry point for all MechMind / Photoneo / Pickit3D vision interface calls.

This is the function a PyFM vision-interface step actually calls; every function above (connect / execute_* / trigger / etc.) is one of this function’s dispatch targets and can also be called directly by SDK users who already hold a client and don’t need the data-driven dispatch. Which sub-function runs is chosen by option and, for Photoneo/Pickit, a “function_code” field inside data (MechMind instead uses a “type” field, see below):

  • “MECHMIND_INTERFACE”: data[“type”] selects “CONNECT” (execute_mechmind_connect), “READ” (function_code 0 = Trigger And Get Poses via execute_mechmind_trigger_and_get_poses, 2 = Get Poses via execute_mechmind_get_poses), or “WRITE” (function_code 1 = Trigger via execute_mechmind_trigger, 3 = Set Recipe via execute_mechmind_set_recipe).

  • ”PHOTONEO_INTERFACE”: data[“function_code”] selects 99 = Create Connection (execute_photoneo_connect), 0/1/4/5/6 = Initialize / Scan / Solution Change / Solution Start / Solution Stop (WRITE), 2/3/7 = Get Object Pose / Get Trajectory / Solution Ask (READ), or 8 = Move (JB) through a stored trajectory (execute_photoneo_move_waypoints, resolving the trajectory by PyFM variable name or an inline waypoint list).

  • ”PICKIT_INTERFACE”: data[“function_code”] selects 99 = Create Connection (execute_pickit_connect), one of 0/2/3/4/5/6/10/13/14/15/16/17/18 for the WRITE-family calls (update robot pose, shutdown, calibration, configure, capture image, …), or one of 1/7/8/9/11/12 for the READ-family calls (check mode, look for objects (with retries), next object, process image, get pick point data).

See each dispatch target’s own docstring above for its payload fields, return value and failure handling — this function only picks which one runs and supplies it with the connection’s client, plus a robot state snapshot for calls that need pose correction.

Note

below), if option is not one of the three vendors, or if the selected type/function_code is not recognized; and whatever the selected dispatch target itself throws.

Note

data[“server_ip”] is required and validated even for calls that reuse an already-open connection (READ/WRITE/etc.) and never use its value — this matches the Python original’s behavior, not a porting oversight.

Note

If alarm_fn is not provided and flow_manager_args is, this function resolves it by looking up “rb_program_sdk.alarm” in the PyFM context’s SDK function registry. If that lookup also fails, or flow_manager_args is not provided either, any “ASK” resolve_option downstream effectively behaves like “SKIP” (no alarm is fired, since alarm_fn stays null).

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model whose state and vision connection this call applies to.

  • option – Vision vendor: “MECHMIND_INTERFACE”, “PHOTONEO_INTERFACE”, or “PICKIT_INTERFACE”.

  • data – Interface payload; its shape depends on option and the selected type/function_code, see above.

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used by any dispatch target whose resolve_option is “ASK”.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. Required for this call to do anything — if omitted, returns immediately without dispatching to any target (unlike the individual execute_* functions below, which work standalone; call one of those directly instead of vision() if PyFM isn’t in play). When provided, it’s forwarded as-is to the selected dispatch target.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If data[“server_ip”] is falsy/missing (required for every call, not just CONNECT — see

RBPluginCall adds the plugin_id prefix, so this class only deals with relative paths/topics. The public API intentionally matches plugin.py: on(), subscribe(), and emit().

(payload, meta) -> reply. Called only after the transport gate passes. Throw PluginRouteError to choose the external response status.

Request payload.

Request metadata, including transport and principal when supplied by the gateway.

Reply payload.

Scopes topic with scoped(). If this is the first local subscription for that topic and the gateway is connected, emits "sub". Keep the returned Subscription and pass it to unsubscribe(topic, sub) to remove only this subscription.

Subscription handle. Keep it and pass it to unsubscribe() to remove only this subscription.

void unsubscribe(const std::optional<std::string> &topic = std::nullopt, const Subscription &sub = Subscription{})#

One-to-one equivalent of plugin.py::unsubscribe.

Both arguments are optional. A valid sub removes only that subscription. Without a valid handle, this removes a topic or all subscriptions.

  • unsubscribe() -> remove all subscriptions

  • unsubscribe(“ui/event”) -> remove all subscriptions on that topic

  • unsubscribe(std::nullopt, s) -> remove only handle s

  • unsubscribe(“ui/event”, s) -> remove s only if it belongs to that topic

Emits "unsub" for each topic that becomes empty. A topic-only unsubscribe also emits when that topic was not registered locally.

Parameters:

  • topic – Optional topic filter. The topic is scoped with scoped().

  • sub – Optional subscription handle to remove.

topic – Topic whose subscriptions should be removed.

class Subscription#
#include <rb_plugin.hpp>

Handle returned by subscribe().

Copyable value type around a globally unique token. This is not RAII: destroying it does not unsubscribe. Pass it to RBPluginCall::unsubscribe(topic, sub) to remove the subscription.

This replaces the plugin.py pattern of passing the callback function back to unsubscribe. The token is meaningful only for the RBPluginCall instance that created it; token() is exposed for bindings.

RpcResult execute_modbus_read(RpcManager &rpc, const std::string &module_name, const std::string &server_ip, int server_port, int function_code, int register_addr, int number_of_read, const std::string &return_variable_name, const std::string &resolve_option = "SKIP", double timeout_sec = 1.0, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr)#

Reads Modbus holding or input registers.

function_code selects the register type: 3 reads holding registers (READ_HOLDING), 4 reads input registers (READ_INPUT).

Parameters:

  • rpc – RpcManager handle for the target connection, obtained via RBProgramSDK::get_rpc(module_name).

  • module_name – PyFM task id identifying the calling step/task.

  • server_ip – Modbus server IP address.

  • server_port – Modbus server port.

  • function_code – 3 (READ_HOLDING) or 4 (READ_INPUT).

  • register_addr – Starting register address to read from.

  • number_of_read – Number of registers to read.

  • return_variable_name – PyFM variable name that will receive the read registers (RpcResult::regs).

  • resolve_option – How to handle a failed read — “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • timeout_sec – Read timeout in seconds. Defaults to 1.0.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. return_variable_name is written into its context and flow_manager_args.done() is called on completion (unless resolve_option is “STOP” and the read failed, which raises instead).

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If function_code is not 3 or 4; and, under “STOP”, if the read fails.

Returns:

RpcResult from the native call (success flag plus the read registers in regs).

RpcResult execute_modbus_write(RpcManager &rpc, const std::string &module_name, const std::string &server_ip, int server_port, int function_code, int register_addr, const std::optional<rb_payload::WriteRegisterValues> &payload_field, const std::string &resolve_option = "SKIP", double timeout_sec = 1.0, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr)#

Writes Modbus holding registers.

function_code selects the write mode: 6 writes a single register (WRITE_SINGLE_REG), 16 writes multiple registers (WRITE_MULTI_REGS).

Parameters:

  • rpc – RpcManager handle for the target connection, obtained via RBProgramSDK::get_rpc(module_name).

  • module_name – PyFM task id identifying the calling step/task.

  • server_ip – Modbus server IP address.

  • server_port – Modbus server port.

  • function_code – 6 (WRITE_SINGLE_REG) or 16 (WRITE_MULTI_REGS).

  • register_addr – Starting register address to write to.

  • payload_field – List of register values to write (1-40 entries, each in [0, 65535]).

  • resolve_option – How to handle a failed write — “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • timeout_sec – Write timeout in seconds. Defaults to 1.0.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. flow_manager_args.done() is called on completion (unless resolve_option is “STOP” and the write failed, which raises instead).

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If function_code is not 6 or 16, or payload_field is missing/out of range; and, under “STOP”, if the write fails.

Returns:

RpcResult from the native call.

RpcResult execute_mc_read(RpcManager &rpc, const std::string &module_name, const std::string &server_ip, int server_port, int register_addr, const std::string &address_type, const std::string &protocol, int function_code, int number_of_read, const std::string &return_variable_name, const std::string &resolve_option = "SKIP", FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr)#

Reads MC (Mitsubishi) protocol device values.

function_code selects the command: 1 reads bit devices (read_bit), 2 reads word devices (read_word). address_type and protocol resolve the target McDeviceType and McFrameType respectively. The result is always taken from RpcResult::data_word — unlike the Python original’s data_word or data_bit fallback, a bit read does not fall back to data_bit (matches the current C++ behavior).

Parameters:

  • rpc – RpcManager handle for the target connection, obtained via RBProgramSDK::get_rpc(module_name).

  • module_name – PyFM task id identifying the calling step/task.

  • server_ip – MC server IP address.

  • server_port – MC server port.

  • register_addr – Starting device address to read from.

  • address_type – Device type: “1”/”D”, “2”/”M”, “3”/”X”, or “4”/”Y”.

  • protocol – MC frame type: “1”/”MC_1E” or “2”/”MC_3E”.

  • function_code – 1 (read_bit) or 2 (read_word).

  • number_of_read – Number of devices to read.

  • return_variable_name – PyFM variable name that will receive the read values (RpcResult::data_word).

  • resolve_option – How to handle a failed read — “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. return_variable_name is written into its context and flow_manager_args.done() is called on completion (unless resolve_option is “STOP” and the read failed, which raises instead).

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If function_code is not 1 or 2, or address_type/protocol cannot be resolved; and, under “STOP”, if the read fails.

Returns:

RpcResult from the native call (success flag plus the read values in data_word).

RpcResult execute_mc_write(RpcManager &rpc, const std::string &module_name, const std::string &server_ip, int server_port, int register_addr, const std::string &address_type, const std::string &protocol, int function_code, const std::optional<rb_payload::WriteRegisterValues> &payload_field, const std::string &resolve_option = "SKIP", FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr)#

Writes MC (Mitsubishi) protocol device values.

function_code selects the command: 3 writes bit devices (write_bit, payload_field values restricted to 0/1), 4 writes word devices (write_word, payload_field values restricted to [-32768, 32767]). address_type also determines which native buffer the payload is sent through: “1”/”D” (word device) uses write_word, “2”/”3”/”4” or “M”/”X”/”Y” (bit devices) use write_bit.

Parameters:

  • rpc – RpcManager handle for the target connection, obtained via RBProgramSDK::get_rpc(module_name).

  • module_name – PyFM task id identifying the calling step/task.

  • server_ip – MC server IP address.

  • server_port – MC server port.

  • register_addr – Starting device address to write to.

  • address_type – Device type: “1”/”D”, “2”/”M”, “3”/”X”, or “4”/”Y”.

  • protocol – MC frame type: “1”/”MC_1E” or “2”/”MC_3E”.

  • function_code – 3 (write_bit) or 4 (write_word).

  • payload_field – List of values to write (1-40 entries), range depends on function_code as described above.

  • resolve_option – How to handle a failed write — “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. flow_manager_args.done() is called on completion (unless resolve_option is “STOP” and the write failed, which raises instead).

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If function_code is not 3 or 4, address_type/protocol cannot be resolved, or payload_field is missing/out of range; and, under “STOP”, if the write fails.

Returns:

RpcResult from the native call.

  • device_type – Device type; only “DB” is currently supported.

  • function_code – Must be 3 (write_byte).

  • payload_field – List of values to write (1-40 entries, each in [-32768, 32767]).

  • resolve_option – How to handle a failed write — “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. flow_manager_args.done() is called on completion (unless resolve_option is “STOP” and the write failed, which raises instead).

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If function_code is not 3, cpu_type/device_type cannot be resolved, or payload_field is missing/out of range; and, under “STOP”, if the write fails.

Returns:

RpcResult from the native call.

RpcResult execute_socket_read(RpcManager &rpc, const std::string &module_name, const std::string &server_ip, int server_port, int function_code, const std::string &return_variable_name, const std::string &resolve_option = "SKIP", double timeout_sec = 1.0, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr)#

Receives data over a socket connection.

function_code selects how the received payload is decoded before being stored: 1 keeps it as the raw byte list, 2 decodes it as a UTF-8 string.

Parameters:

  • rpc – RpcManager handle for the target connection, obtained via RBProgramSDK::get_rpc(module_name).

  • module_name – PyFM task id identifying the calling step/task.

  • server_ip – Socket server IP address.

  • server_port – Socket server port.

  • function_code – 1 (raw bytes) or 2 (UTF-8 string).

  • return_variable_name – PyFM variable name that will receive the decoded payload.

  • resolve_option – How to handle a failed receive — “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • timeout_sec – Receive timeout in seconds. Defaults to 1.0.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. return_variable_name is written into its context and flow_manager_args.done() is called on completion (unless resolve_option is “STOP” and the receive failed, which raises instead).

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If function_code is not 1 or 2, or the payload cannot be decoded as UTF-8; and, under “STOP”, if the receive fails.

Returns:

RpcResult from the native call (success flag plus the raw payload in payload).

RpcResult execute_socket_write(RpcManager &rpc, const std::string &module_name, const std::string &server_ip, int server_port, int function_code, const std::string &payload, const std::string &resolve_option = "SKIP", FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr)#

Sends data over a socket connection.

function_code selects how payload is encoded before sending: 3 (BYTES) splits payload on the delimiter read from flow_manager_args.args["data"]["split"] and parses each token as an integer byte value; 4 (ASCII) encodes payload directly as ASCII bytes.

Parameters:

  • rpc – RpcManager handle for the target connection, obtained via RBProgramSDK::get_rpc(module_name).

  • module_name – PyFM task id identifying the calling step/task.

  • server_ip – Socket server IP address.

  • server_port – Socket server port.

  • function_code – 3 (BYTES, delimiter-split) or 4 (ASCII).

  • payload – String payload to send; interpretation depends on function_code as described above.

  • resolve_option – How to handle a failed send — “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context, required when function_code is 3 to look up the split delimiter. flow_manager_args.done() is called on completion (unless resolve_option is “STOP” and the send failed, which raises instead).

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If function_code is not 3 or 4, the BYTES split delimiter is missing, or payload cannot be parsed/encoded; and, under “STOP”, if the send fails.

Returns:

RpcResult from the native call.

bool execute_socket_connect(RpcManager &rpc, const std::string &module_name, const std::string &server_ip, int server_port, const std::string &resolve_option = "SKIP", FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, AlarmFn alarm_fn = nullptr)#

Opens a socket connection and registers the session under module_name.

Only creates the session (connect_sock()); it does not wait for a response, so unlike the other execute_* calls in this file the GIL is not released while the call runs.

Parameters:

  • rpc – RpcManager handle for the target connection, obtained via RBProgramSDK::get_rpc(module_name).

  • module_name – PyFM task id identifying the calling step/task.

  • server_ip – Socket server IP address.

  • server_port – Socket server port.

  • resolve_option – How to handle a failed connect — “SKIP” continues without effect, “STOP” raises immediately, “ASK” fires alarm_fn and pauses the PyFM context (requires flow_manager_args). Defaults to “SKIP”.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. flow_manager_args.done() is called on completion (unless resolve_option is “STOP” and the connect failed, which raises instead).

  • alarm_fn – Optional (title, content) callback used only when resolve_option is “ASK”.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – Under “STOP”, if the connect fails.

Returns:

true if the connection was established; false otherwise.

void set_variables(const nlohmann::json &variables, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Initializes local task variables from their configured init values.

Parameters:

  • variables – List of variable definition dicts, each carrying an “init_value” key, in the same order as the task’s declared variables.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. Required for this call to do anything — if omitted, returns immediately without touching variables. When provided, each variable is applied via flow_manager_args's local variable updater and the step is marked done afterwards.

void make_script(const std::string &mode, std::optional<std::string> contents, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Runs a program script step, in either GENERAL or ADVANCED mode.

In GENERAL mode, flow_manager_args's “general_contents” argument is evaluated as a single expression against the step’s context (assignments are reflected into state). In ADVANCED mode, contents is compiled and executed as an arbitrary python script with variables/var, update_variable, update_var/update, get_var/get, done, pause, stop, resume, check_stop, and rb_log injected into its globals (the bridge builds that env from flow_manager_args; compile/exec runs on the PyFM side in ctx.run_advanced_script). rb_log is this SDK’s own log (RBBaseSDK::log), called as rb_log(content, robot_model, level).

Parameters:

  • mode – “GENERAL” or “ADVANCED”.

  • contents – ADVANCED-mode script source. Required when mode is “ADVANCED”.

  • flow_manager_args – PyFM step context. Required; the step is marked done when the script finishes (or immediately raises, in ADVANCED mode, since the step is still marked done before the exception propagates).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If GENERAL mode is missing “general_contents”, or ADVANCED mode is missing contents.

void simple_wait(double second, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Blocks the calling thread for second seconds, polling for stop/pause requests every 1/50s. Time spent blocked inside a pause is excluded from the wait duration.

Parameters:

  • second – Seconds to wait. Must be greater than 0 when flow_manager_args is not provided (a standalone caller has no other way to be notified that the wait was skipped).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. If provided, the step is marked done once the wait elapses (or immediately, if second <= 0).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If second <= 0 and flow_manager_args is not provided.

void alarm_or_halt(const std::string &robot_model, const std::string &option, bool save_log, bool is_only_at_ui, const std::string &pause_option, const nlohmann::json &title, const nlohmann::json &content, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Raises an alarm and/or halts execution, depending on option.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • option – “ALARM” (publish an alarm dialog), “HALT” (stop the step’s context), “FOLDER_HALT” (break out of the enclosing folder), or “SUB_PROGRAM_HALT” (halt the enclosing sub task).

  • save_log – If true, also emits a USER-level log entry with content (or title if content is None).

  • is_only_at_ui – If true and the step is not running from a UI execution, the step is marked done and this call is a no-op.

  • pause_option – “ALL” (pause every process) or “CURRENT” (pause only this context). Only consulted when option resolves to a pause.

  • title – Alarm dialog title (used when option is “ALARM”, and as the log fallback content when save_log is set and content is None).

  • content – Alarm dialog / log content.

  • flow_manager_args – PyFM step context. Required; the step is marked done after the alarm/halt/pause sequence completes.

void debug_variables(const std::string &robot_model, const std::string &option, bool is_only_at_ui, const nlohmann::json &variables, const nlohmann::json &log_content, const std::string &pause_option, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Reports the current values of variables for debugging, then pauses.

Compares each variable’s raw (pre-evaluation) string against its evaluated JSON value; numeric values/lists are rounded to 3 decimals for display, and unchanged variables are reported as “Undefined”.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • option – “DIALOG” (publish a single alarm dialog listing every variable) or “LOG” (emit one USER-level log entry per variable).

  • is_only_at_ui – If true and the step is not running from a UI execution, the step is marked done and this call is a no-op.

  • variables – Evaluated current variable values, in the same order as flow_manager_args's raw “variables” list.

  • log_content – Optional extra USER-level log entry (any value; non-str is JSON-encoded) appended after the per-variable LOG entries.

  • pause_option – “ALL” (pause every process) or “CURRENT” (pause only this context).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. Required for this call to do anything; the step is marked done after pausing.

void user_input(const std::string &robot_model, const nlohmann::json &var_selection, const std::string &var_form, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Publishes a “user input” prompt dialog and pauses the step until the operator supplies a value (resumed out-of-band via the program service’s change_user_input_value endpoint).

Mirrors program.py::RBProgramSDK.user_input: the dialog content is "{raw var_selection arg} ({resolved var_selection})" — the raw name comes from flow_manager_args.args["var_selection"] (pre-substitution) and the resolved value from the var_selection parameter.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • var_form – Input widget kind: “STRING” (default), “NUMERIC”, “BOOLEAN”, “LIST”, “DICTIONARY”, or “VAR”. Only used to tag the alarm title (USER_INPUT_{var_form}).

  • var_selection – Resolved value of the target variable. PyFM evaluates the step’s var_selection expression before the call, so this can arrive as any Python type (int/float/list/dict, …), not only str — it is stringified here, mirroring the Python original’s f-string.

  • flow_manager_args – PyFM step context. When provided, the step’s context is paused, checked for stop, and marked done.

void user_select(const std::string &robot_model, const nlohmann::json &ask_ment, const nlohmann::json &var_name, const nlohmann::json &content, const nlohmann::json &timeout, const nlohmann::json &disconn_timeout, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Publishes a “user select” prompt dialog and pauses the step until the operator picks one of content (resumed out-of-band via the program service’s set_user_select_value endpoint).

Mirrors program.py::RBProgramSDK.user_select: the dialog content is json.dumps([var_name, timeout, disconn_timeout, content]).

Note

ask_ment/var_name/content/timeout/disconn_timeout arrive as values PyFM produced by evaluating the step’s args, so their runtime types are not fixed (e.g. a "60" arg resolves to int 60, "0" to int 0). They are accepted as JSON values and normalized to the expected C++ type before serialization.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model.

  • ask_ment – Prompt text, used to tag the alarm title (USER_SELECT_{ask_ment}).

  • var_name – Name of the variable that will receive the choice.

  • content – Selectable option strings.

  • timeout – Seconds before the select auto-resolves.

  • disconn_timeout – Behavior label when the operator UI disconnects.

  • flow_manager_args – PyFM step context. When provided, the step’s context is paused, checked for stop, and marked done.

void interface(const std::string &option, muscat::InterfacePayloadUnion data, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Dispatches a protocol interface call (Modbus/MC/XGT/socket) via the native RpcManager cached for this step’s task id (rpc_managers_).

Parameters:

  • option – “MODBUS_CLIENT”, “MC_PROTOCOL”, “XGT_PROTOCOL”, or “SOCKET_INTERFACE”.

  • data – Protocol payload generated from manipulate.fbs. Must contain a non-empty “server_ip” and a “type” of “READ”/”WRITE” (plus “CONNECT” for SOCKET_INTERFACE).

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. Required for this call to do anything — if omitted, returns immediately without dispatching to any protocol. When provided, it’s forwarded to the underlying execute_* call and the step is marked done after dispatch.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If option or data[“type”] is unsupported for the given option.

void wait(const std::string &robot_model, const std::string &wait_type, const std::string &mode, std::optional<double> second, std::optional<ProgramDigitalInputCondition> digital_input, std::optional<double> time_out, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Blocks until the requested wait condition is satisfied (or times out), polling for stop requests every 10ms.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – Name of the robot model (used for DIGITAL_INPUT polling).

  • wait_type – “TIME” (delegates to simple_wait()), “HOLDING” (wait while the condition holds), or “EXIT” (wait until the condition becomes true / the digital input matches).

  • mode – “GENERAL” (evaluate flow_manager_args's “condition” expression) or “DIGITAL_INPUT” (poll get_digital_input() against digital_input's expected signal pattern).

  • second – Wait duration in seconds, used only when wait_type is “TIME”.

  • digital_input – Digital input condition dict (“signal” list and optional “logical_operator”, “AND” by default). Required when mode is “DIGITAL_INPUT”.

  • time_out – Optional timeout in seconds; the wait loop breaks once elapsed time reaches this value, regardless of whether the condition was satisfied.

  • flow_manager_args – Optional PyFM step context. Required for this call to do anything — if omitted, returns immediately without waiting (despite the default of py::none(), calling this standalone is a no-op). The step is marked done once the wait loop exits.

void change_program(std::optional<std::string> program_id, std::optional<std::string> program_name, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr)#

Changes the running program and immediately starts it (program.py::change_program).

Sends a Request_Change_Program to the “muscat/change/program” queryable and waits (up to 20s — the handler can take several seconds) for a ResponseProgramExecution. Either program_id or program_name must be given.

Parameters:

  • program_id – Target program id (mutually optional with program_name).

  • program_name – Target program name.

  • flow_manager_args – PyFM step context. Required — raises if omitted. The step is marked done once the change is accepted.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If flow_manager_args is omitted, if neither program_id nor program_name is given, or if the change/start request gets no (usable) reply.

void plugin_execute(const std::string &plugin_id, FlowManagerArgsPtr flow_manager_args = nullptr, const nlohmann::json &user_args = nlohmann::json::object())#

Sends an execute request to a plugin process and waits until it reports completion (or stop). Concurrent calls for the same plugin_id are serialized so their control queryables don’t collide.

Parameters:

  • plugin_id – Target plugin id; the request is sent to “muscat/plugin/{plugin_id}/execute” and control messages are exchanged over “muscat/plugin/{plugin_id}/control”.

  • user_args – Execute request JSON object. The Python binding collects **kwargs into this object.

  • flow_manager_args – PyFM step context. Required; the step is marked done once the plugin reports “done” (directly, or by exiting its control loop after “stop”).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If flow_manager_args is not provided, or if the plugin is not running/responding to the execute request.

class RBRby1CommandHandle#
#include <rb_rby1_sdk.hpp>

로봇 명령 핸들 (RBRby1SDK.send_command 결과, 공식 RobotCommandHandler 래퍼).

블로킹 메서드(wait/get)는 기본 async, handle.sync.<method> 는 동기다. 핸들을 버리면 명령이 취소된다 (공식 소멸자 = Cancel) — 명령이 끝날 때까지 핸들을 쥐고 있어야 한다. async wait/get 을 기다리던 쪽이 취소되면(Task.cancel, asyncio.wait_for 타임아웃, 루프 종료) 결과만 버리지 않고 로봇 명령도 취소한다 (cancel()). 이때 flow_manager_args.done() 은 부르지 않는다. disconnect_robot 뒤에도 이미 보낸 명령의 wait/get/is_done/cancel 은 그 명령에 대해 동작한다. fork 자식에서는 부모의 핸들을 쓸 수 없다 (RBY1ConnectionError, cancel 은 할 일 없음).

class RBRby1SerialStream#
#include <rb_rby1_sdk.hpp>

로봇 시리얼 장치 스트림 (RBRby1SDK.open_serial_stream 결과, 공식 SerialStream 래퍼).

connect() 후 write() 로 보내고, 받은 데이터는 open_serial_stream 의 callback(data: bytes) 으로 온다. 콜백은 수신 전용 스레드에서 순서대로 한 번에 하나씩 불린다 (gRPC 수신은 막히지 않는다 — 콜백이 느리면 1024 chunk 까지 쌓고, 넘치면 오래된 것부터 버린다: read_stats 의 dropped). 콜백이 awaitable 을 돌려주면 등록 시점의 이벤트 루프에서 실행하고 끝날 때까지 다음 chunk 를 넘기지 않는다. 콜백 예외는 stderr 로 출력한다. 블로킹 메서드는 기본 async, stream.sync.<method> 는 동기다. async 호출을 기다리던 쪽이 취소되면 스트림을 끊는다 (cancel()). 핸들을 버리면 스트림이 끊긴다 (공식 소멸자). disconnect_robot / connect_robot 뒤에는 connect/write 를 보내지 않는다 (RBY1ConnectionError).

인스턴스는 얇은 핸들이고 로봇 gRPC 연결은 프로세스에 하나다 — 몇 번 생성해도 같은 연결을 쓴다. Python 에서 메서드는 기본 async (gRPC 대기를 C++ worker 스레드에서 GIL 없이), sdk.sync.<method> 는 동기. 로봇 연결은 connect_robot/disconnect_robot 이다 — RBBaseSDK.connect/disconnect 는 zenoh 원격 peer 등록.

static std::string connect_robot(const std::optional<std::string> &endpoint = std::nullopt, const std::optional<std::string> &model = std::nullopt, int max_retries = 5, int timeout_ms = 1000)#

RB-Y1 gRPC 서버에 연결하고 로봇 model 을 확정한다.

이미 같은 endpoint(기본값 해석 후)·같은 model(생략 시 무관)로 연결돼 있고 채널이 살아 있으면 no-op — 연결과 스트림을 그대로 두고 연결된 model 을 반환한다. 그 밖에는 기존 연결·스트림을 끊고 새로 연결한다.

Parameters:

  • endpoint – “host:port”. None 이면 환경변수 RBY1_HOST(없으면 192.168.30.1) + “:50051”.

  • model – “a” / “m” / “ub”. 주면 그 model 이 아닐 때 실패한다. 생략하면 로봇이 알려준 model.

  • max_retries – 연결 재시도 횟수.

  • timeout_ms – 시도당 타임아웃(ms).

Throws:

RBY1ConnectionError – 연결 실패 또는 model 불일치.

Returns:

연결된 model 이름 (“a” / “m” / “ub”).

static void start_state_update(const std::string &robot_model, rby1_rt::StateSink callback, double rate)#

로봇 상태 스트림을 시작한다 (latest-only).

공식 start_state_update 와 같이 콜백 인자는 1개 또는 2개다: callback(state) 또는 callback(state, control_manager_state). 개수는 등록 때 한 번 inspect.signature(callback).parameters 로 센다 (bound method 의 self, partial 로 묶인 인자는 빠진다). 그 밖의 개수면 TypeError. 두 값은 같은 스트림 샘플 (GetRobotStateStream 응답 하나)에서 온다 — 1개 형도 같은 RPC 이므로 비용 차이는 없다.

콜백은 스트림 전용 스레드에서 한 번에 하나씩 불린다. 콜백이 느리면 그 사이 도착한 상태는 최신 것만 남고 나머지는 버린다 (gRPC 수신은 막히지 않는다). 콜백이 awaitable(코루틴 등)을 돌려주면 등록 시점의 실행 중 이벤트 루프에서 실행하고 끝날 때까지 다음 상태를 넘기지 않는다 (코루틴도 latest-only). 코루틴 함수를 이벤트 루프 밖에서 등록하면 RuntimeError, 그 밖의 콜백이 루프 없이 awaitable 을 돌려주면 에러 로그 후 그 상태를 버린다. 콜백 예외는 stderr 로 출력하고 스트림은 계속된다. 같은 model 로 다시 부르면 이전 스트림을 멈추고 새로 시작한다. 콜백 안에서 stop_state_update 를 불러도 된다.

끊김 복구: 공식 SDK 는 서버가 스트림을 끝내도 알리지 않으므로, max(10/rate, 1)초 동안 상태가 안 오면 다시 구독한다 (stderr 에 끊김·복구 한 줄씩, 재시도 간격은 두 배씩 4배까지, state_update_stats 의 resubscribes). gRPC 연결은 공식 채널이 스스로 다시 맺으므로 로봇이 돌아오면 connect_robot 없이 스트림이 이어진다.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – 로봇 model (“a” / “m” / “ub”). 연결된 로봇과 다르면 실패.

  • callback – callback(state) 또는 callback(state, control_manager_state) — state 는 rby1.RobotState_A / _M / _UB, control_manager_state 는 rby1.ControlManagerState (공식 타입).

  • rate – 요청 수신 주기(Hz).

Throws:

RBY1Error – model 불일치. RBY1ConnectionError 미연결. TypeError 콜백 인자 개수가 1·2 가 아님.

Parameters:

static RBRby1CommandHandle send_command(const std::string &robot_model, RBRby1CommandBuilderRef builder, int priority = 1)#

로봇 명령을 보낸다 (수락까지만 — 완료는 핸들의 wait/get 으로 기다린다).

명령 완료가 PyFM step 완료이므로 flow_manager_args 는 핸들의 wait/get 에 넘긴다. 반환된 핸들을 버리면 명령이 취소된다 (공식 핸들 소멸자). await 가 실행 전에 취소되면 명령은 보내지 않는다.

Parameters:

  • robot_model – 로봇 model (“a” / “m” / “ub”). 연결된 로봇과 다르면 실패.

  • builder – rby1.RobotCommandBuilder (공식 타입).

  • priority – 명령 우선순위 (높을수록 우선).

Throws:

RBY1Error – 호출 실패. RBY1ConnectionError 미연결.

Returns:

RBRby1CommandHandle.

static RBRby1SerialStream open_serial_stream(const std::string &robot_model, const std::string &device_path, int baudrate, int bytesize = 8, char parity = 'N', int stopbits = 1, rby1_rt::SerialSink callback = nullptr)#

로봇의 시리얼 장치 스트림을 연다 (장치는 반환된 스트림의 connect() 로 연다).

Parameters:

  • robot_model – 로봇 model (“a” / “m” / “ub”). 연결된 로봇과 다르면 실패.

  • device_path – 장치 경로 (get_serial_device_list 의 path).

  • baudrate – 보드레이트.

  • bytesize – 데이터 비트 수.

  • parity – 패리티 (‘N’ / ‘E’ / ‘O’).

  • stopbits – 스톱 비트 수.

  • callback – callback(data: bytes) — 받은 데이터. 수신 전용 스레드에서 순서대로 불린다. None 이면 받지 않는다.

Throws:

RBY1Error – 호출 실패. RBY1ConnectionError 미연결.

Returns:

RBRby1SerialStream.
